candidates.title: HTIF console-getchar reproducibility guard runs only at create/load: after write_reg("htif_iconsole") native run diverges from the uarch and collect_mcycle_root_hashes, host console input reaches a reproducible machine's hashed state, and store writes a directory that refuses to load
candidates.component: Emulator core: machine::init_console / machine::write_reg / machine::set_runtime_config / machine::write_memory (full-shadow path), native state_access getchar vs. non-interactive state accesses (uarch, collectors, replay)
candidates.role: The write_reg / set_runtime_config / write_memory calls are 'the rest of the machine API' (off the honest operator's path for these registers/options). The paths that diverge (native interpreter via run, uarch, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, store/load) are honest-operator components per the AUDIT.md table.
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp: init_console() (~351-358) is the only place that refuses an enabled HTIF getchar (hashed register htif_iconsole) or a non-null console input source (runtime config) on a reproducible machine, and it runs only from the constructor (create and load). machine::write_reg case reg::htif_iconsole (~1468) writes the hashed register with no check; machine::set_runtime_config (~415-424) replaces m_r.console with no reproducibility check; machine::write_memory full-shadow path (~1846-1860) calls validate_processor_shadow, which checks iunrep but not iconsole. src/htif-address-range.cpp htif_console(): GETCHAR calls a->getchar(). src/device-state-access.hpp do_getchar(): interactive accesses (native state_access) forward to machine_console::getchar, non-interactive ones (uarch_state_access/uarch bridge, collect_mcycle_hashes_state_access, record/replay) return -1. src/machine-console.cpp open_input(): from_null sets m_input_closed = true, and getchars() then returns END_OF_TRANSMISSION_CHAR (4). machine::store (~430) checks only is_unreproducible() (config copy).
candidates.description: Same root cause as R1-R2-1 at another site: whether the HTIF console getchar command may be honoured in a reproducible machine is decided by a hashed register (htif_iconsole, getchar bit) plus a runtime option (console input source), but the guard that keeps both off in reproducible machines (init_console: 'TTY stdin is only supported in unreproducible machines') is evaluated once, at construction. Afterwards (a) write_reg("htif_iconsole", v|1) (also write_word at its address, or a full-shadow write_memory) enables getchar in a reproducible machine, and (b) set_runtime_config can switch the console input source to from_buffer/from_file/from_fd/from_stdin. Once getchar is enabled, the transition of an mcycle that executes a GETCHAR tohost write depends on which state access runs it: the native interpreter (machine::run) asks the host console and writes fromhost DATA = c+1 (5 for the default closed from_null input, i.e. EOT; or host-supplied bytes after (b)), while the uarch, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, collect_*_bundle and the log producers/verifiers return -1 and write DATA = 0. So two honest-operator paths compute different hashes from the same state (R2), host input enters the hashed state of a reproducible machine (R14), and machine::store (which checks only the config copy of iunrep) succeeds and writes a directory that its own load refuses with 'TTY stdin is only supported in unreproducible machines' (R9 / Medium case on stored directories). The manual describes iconsole only as an initial value ('The processor.registers.htif sub-table holds the initial values of HTIF state'; '-i' is a creation option) and says verifiable computations must run non-interactively.
candidates.trigger: A trusted machine-API caller (local, Lua or JSON-RPC) calls write_reg("htif_iconsole", value with bit HTIF_CONSOLE_CMD_GETCHAR) on a reproducible machine (optionally also set_runtime_config with a non-null console input source), then runs a guest that issues an HTIF console GETCHAR, or stores the machine. No guest or input can trigger it: the HTIF device accepts guest writes only to tohost and fromhost, and delivery never touches iconsole.
candidates.reachability: Not reachable from a valid template by inputs: a reproducible machine with getchar enabled is refused at creation and at load (init_console reads the hashed iconsole), and no instruction or delivery writes iconsole (htif_address_range::do_write_device accepts only tohost/fromhost). The split state is reachable only through the documented machine-API write, exactly as for R1-R2-1. So no honest-operator path from a valid template reaches it.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Exclusion 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented (section 4)' covers the component but, as argued for R1-R2-1, not the defect: the documented effect is that the register changes; the emulator then honouring host console input in a reproducible machine on one path only, and store writing a directory its own load refuses, are not documented effects of that write. 'Defects that need an untrusted party to call the machine API directly' does not apply (trusted caller). No snapshot/O1/O2 exclusion applies (the emulator wrote the directory; no stop, no sharing). 2. Role: write_reg/set_runtime_config are 'the rest of the machine API', honest operator only 'where a production validator node plausibly calls it on the honest operator's path'; no node writes htif_iconsole or switches a reproducible machine's console input, so the triggering use is off-path. The diverging components (native interpreter, uarch, collect_mcycle_root_hashes, store/load) are honest operator. 3. High/Medium cases: Medium 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves the hash tree, the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)': store writes a directory (config.json + shadow with getchar enabled, iunrep 0) that load refuses. The R2 divergence ('Wherever two of the following reach the same position, they must agree on its canonical hash: Native interpretation; The uarch running the interpreter...; The computation-hash builders') occurs only at a state no input sequence from a valid template produces; High 'A divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states' could be argued, but the state is reached by API use rather than being demonstrably unreachable in the sense of section 8, which is why I prefer the Medium reading used for R1-R2-1. Also violated: R14 'In a reproducible machine, the host reaches the state only through deliveries and deliberate changes through the machine API. That rules out host devices, any other host input' (console bytes after set_runtime_config are host input, not a deliberate API state change) and R1 'No configuration, runtime option, or file outside the hashed state ... may change any transition' (the console input source, a runtime option, changes the GETCHAR transition natively). 4. Critical: not reached; no reachable state or honest-path operation shows it. 5. Alternative readings: Low ('a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller') if writing a register that the manual describes only as an initial value counts as misuse; Out of scope if the deliberate-change exclusion is read to cover every consequence; High if the R2 divergence is rated as 'a divergence between paths only at demonstrably unreachable states'. The deciding facts are the same as for R1-R2-1.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (preferred, as R1-R2-1); High under the 'divergence at unreachable state' reading; Low/Out of scope under the misuse/deliberate-change readings
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not break the goal of section 1 (no valid template or input reaches it). It violates R2 ('Every register and every configuration value that affects a transition has one source of truth in the hashed state, and every path reads it from there' -- here the reproducibility decision is a creation-time check and the GETCHAR result depends on host console state outside the hash), R14 and R1, and leaves a stored directory that cannot be loaded. A tool, debugger or integration that enables getchar on a reproducible machine silently gets native hashes that no uarch/verifier/collector reproduces, i.e. claims that cannot be proven, and snapshots it cannot reload.
candidates.evidence: Ran two Lua experiments with the in-tree build (bugs/env.sh), scratch files in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r3/VARSHADOW/ (getchar.S assembled with llvm-mc into getchar.bin: tohost <- console GETCHAR, a0 <- fromhost, halt; exp1.lua, exp2.lua). exp1: creating the machine with iconsole getchar enabled is refused ('TTY stdin is only supported in unreproducible machines'); on a reproducible machine (iunrep 0, iconsole 2) write_reg('htif_iconsole', 3) is accepted; native run -> fromhost 0x0100000000000005, a0 = 0x0100000000000005; run_uarch+reset_uarch per mcycle -> fromhost 0x0100000000000000; collect_mcycle_root_hashes -> fromhost 0x0100000000000000; root hashes: native==uarch false, native==collect false, uarch==collect true (all at mcycle 7, halted). store succeeded; loading the stored directory failed with 'TTY stdin is only supported in unreproducible machines'. exp2: creating with console input_source from_buffer is refused, but set_runtime_config({console={input_source='from_buffer'}}) on the reproducible machine succeeds; after write_reg('htif_iconsole', 3) and write_console_input('A'), run puts fromhost DATA 0x42 ('A'+1) into the hashed state.
candidates.test_idea: bugs/<ID>/test.lua: build the 7-instruction guest above (or ship getchar.bin), create a reproducible machine, attempt write_reg('htif_iconsole', iconsole | 1<<HTIF_CONSOLE_CMD_GETCHAR) and set_runtime_config({console={input_source='from_buffer'}}). Exit 0 if both are refused, or if, once accepted, (a) native run, run_uarch+reset_uarch and collect_mcycle_root_hashes reach the same root hash at the halt, (b) host console input does not reach the state (fromhost DATA equal across paths after write_console_input), and (c) store either refuses or writes a directory that loads back with the same root hash. Exit 1 otherwise (currently: native/uarch mismatch, host byte in fromhost, and load refusal).

not_covered: Enumerated, read and found single-source (no candidate): the native interpreter, uarch bridge, uarch_state_access, collect_mcycle/uarch state accesses and replay accesses read every register, the revert root hash, imcyclemax, iflags, HTIF ihalt/iyield/iconsole, CLINT mtimecmp and PLIC girqpend/girqsrvd from the hashed shadow; PMA entries: native uses machine_address_ranges objects, uarch/replay the hashed PMA table, kept equal because the table is protected from host writes (write_memory/fill_memory/write_word refuse protected ranges), replace_memory_range preserves start/length/flags, and load memcmp-checks the table; hot TLB (penumbra) is derived from the shadow TLB on promotion and reset by init_hot_tlb_contents on load, full-shadow write and replace_memory_range, and write_unverified_tlb/write_verified_tlb update both; collector uarch reset uses uarch_registers_state{} whose default initializers equal UARCH_*_INIT; devices (CLINT/PLIC/HTIF) are stateless objects; DTB rng-seed is a constant; soft_yield only adds break points (collectors refuse it).
machine::write_reg still has no read-only guard for iunrep (R1-R2-1, not re-reported) and the full-shadow write_memory path validates iunrep but not iconsole (folded into the candidate).

Unhashed config.json fields of an adopted template other than phtc_size (R1-O1-2): backing_store.shared/hash_tree.shared with CM_SHARING_CONFIG loads (Lua and JSON-RPC load default to SHARING_NONE, so only explicit SHARING_CONFIG writes into the template's files; documented API, not reported), dtb strings, labels, mark_pages_dirty: read only.

skip_version_check runtime option together with the full-shadow write_memory path (lets a host write a different marchid/mimpid into a running machine although write_reg refuses them): noticed, judged a deliberate API change, not pursued.

PRT player values kept outside the machine (pair.revert_root_hash, cache entry root_hash, epoch_stopped, input_count/output_count, forests, state.json) were read for consistency with the hashed state along the run/prove paths only; the restart path (reopen_epoch_directory, revert_interrupted_input) and agreed-pair advancement were not traced under this angle.

cartesi-machine CLI reads iunrep/iconsole/iyield/hash_function from get_initial_config (creation-time config copy, also for loaded machines); equal to the hashed registers unless write_reg changed them, so only the R1-R2-1/candidate root cause; not reported separately.
Solidity step / Dave constants versus emulator constants (left to earlier A6/R13 checks); JSON-RPC client/server hold no cached machine values (checked jsonrpc-machine.hpp members only).
No sanitizer build, no EVM run of the GETCHAR mcycle (the uarch path was run natively; the Solidity step would follow the uarch path since it has no console).
